plan.title: Add a bounded Node web pack for runtime routes, workspace dependency locks and environment key names

criteria.description: The web manifest loads routes/dependencies/env surfaces and a build check with explicit tool/platform requirements.

A built-in Node HTTP sample uses the same route registry as its deterministic export; fixture tests detect route removal, local workspace lock dependency changes and environment key changes, while environment value changes leave exported key data unchanged.

Missing or stale exports, duplicate routes or environment keys, malformed or mismatched lockfiles, unsupported link targets, failed or cancelled builds and concurrent builds fail closed; private environment values and arbitrary resolved URLs do not enter snapshots or diagnostics. CLI execution tests verify missing declared tools produce not-run for the build check and failed/nonpassing extraction, without reusing prior passing evidence.

limitations: Only the public Node 22.22.2/npm 10.9.7 example, npm lockfileVersion 3, explicit static route registry and local workspace dependency are supported. No universal framework, bundler, dynamic router or deployed-service scanner.

Core Go behavior and Go dependencies remain unchanged. Node and Python use standard libraries. No third-party runtime npm dependency is required; local npm workspace installation uses offline, ignore-scripts, no-audit and no-fund settings.

Environment extraction reads only the committed synthetic .env.example and publishes key names, never process environment values or private .env files. Supported grammar is explicit and rejects duplicate/ambiguous input.

Default gate tests use bounded fixtures. Task completion additionally requires actual npm workspace preparation, Node build/test, loopback HTTP registry agreement, repeated deterministic extraction and route/dependency/key mutation plus restoration evidence bound to the code revision.
A build/export pass does not enforce approved surface equality. Existing baseline commands remain the explicit review and approval path; no automatic approvals in the working project.

No deployment, package publication, registry credentials, global settings edits, push, tags or releases. Synthetic lockfile and example values are public; external URLs and local absolute paths are not exported.
